title: IBDP Subject Choices for Medical Students
summary: Choose the right IB subjects for medicine: Biology and Chemistry HL, third-HL options, maths choices, country rules, and practical planning advice.
body_markdown:
For most students planning to study medicine, the safest IBDP subject choices are **Biology HL, Chemistry HL, and a third HL subject in which you can earn a strong grade** . This combination supports the prerequisites of many medical schools while preserving flexibility across countries.


It is not universal. Oxford requires Chemistry HL plus Biology, Physics, or Mathematics at HL, while UCL and Imperial specify Biology and Chemistry at HL. Cambridge requirements can vary by college, and some national systems may require three sciences. Check the official requirements for every country, university, and intended entry year before finalizing your subjects.


### The best general IBDP subject combination for medicine


A strong default programme is:


-


**HL Biology**


-


**HL Chemistry**


-


**HL Mathematics, Physics, Psychology, English, or another strong subject**


-


**SL Mathematics** , unless a target course requires it at HL


-


Two remaining SL subjects that complete the Diploma structure


Biology and Chemistry HL keep a broad range of direct-entry medical options open. Your third HL should satisfy any additional prerequisite while allowing you to maintain a competitive total score.


The IB provides an illustrative medicine combination containing **Chemistry HL, Biology HL, and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL** . However, its[example Diploma subject choices](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/example-subject-choices/) are examples rather than admissions guarantees. Universities determine their own conditions.


### Why Biology and Chemistry HL are usually safest


### Chemistry HL is frequently a formal prerequisite


Chemistry is often the principal gatekeeping subject for medicine. Topics such as bonding, energetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, organic reactions, and analytical methods also support later work in biochemistry, pharmacology, and physiology.


For 2027 entry,[Oxford Medicine](https://www.medsci.ox.ac.uk/study/medicine/pre-clinical/requirements/academic) requires Chemistry HL plus at least one of Biology, Physics, or Mathematics at HL. Biology HL is therefore not mandatory at Oxford when another approved subject is offered, but taking it preserves access to universities that require both sciences.


### Biology HL is required by some medical schools


Biology HL develops knowledge of cells, genetics, metabolism, homeostasis, physiology, and experimental analysis. It also trains students to interpret unfamiliar biological data and explain complex processes precisely.


For 2027 entry,[UCL Medicine](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/medical-sciences/divisions/medical-school/study/undergraduate/mbbs-admissions/entry-requirements/2027-entry) requires Biology and Chemistry at HL. Its standard conditional offer is 39 points, with the three HL subjects totalling at least 19 and Biology and Chemistry graded 6 and 7 in either order.[Imperial Medicine](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/courses/undergraduate/2027/medicine/) also specifies Biology and Chemistry in its admissions expectations.


### Choosing the third Higher Level subject


The third HL should meet any remaining requirement and give you a realistic chance of achieving a high grade. Medical schools generally value exact subject eligibility and excellent results more than an unnecessarily difficult combination.


Third HL option


Main advantage


Important limitation


Mathematics AA


Strong quantitative preparation and useful for science-heavy alternatives


Demanding and not required by most medical schools


Mathematics AI


Develops statistics, modelling, and data interpretation


Some quantitative backup degrees may not accept it


Physics


Preserves physical-science and engineering options


Produces a demanding laboratory-science workload


Psychology


Relevant to behaviour, cognition, and mental health


Cannot replace Biology or Chemistry where required


English or humanities


Provides balance and rewards strong writing skills


May not satisfy universities requiring three science or mathematics HLs


A student who excels in English may be better served by Biology, Chemistry, and English at HL than by forcing Mathematics HL and losing Diploma points. Conversely, some Cambridge applicants may need Biology, Chemistry, and Mathematics or Physics.


The[Cambridge Medicine requirements](https://www.undergraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/medicine-mb-bchir) state that applicants need Chemistry and one or two other subjects from Biology, Mathematics, Physics, or Further Mathematics at A level or IB Higher Level, depending on the college. Applicants must therefore check individual college requirements.


### Should medical students take Mathematics AA or AI?


There is no worldwide rule that medical applicants must take **Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches** , and Mathematics HL is not automatically necessary. If shortlisted courses do not specify a mathematics route, choose the option in which you can perform strongly while protecting access to relevant backup degrees.


Mathematics AA is generally safer for alternatives such as engineering, physics, or mathematically intensive sciences. Mathematics AI can be appropriate where universities accept it and the student is stronger in statistics, modelling, and applied contexts. Oxford states that it has no preference between AA and AI when Mathematics HL is used to satisfy its Medicine subject requirement, but other institutions may treat them differently.


### When three sciences may be necessary


Under the standard[IB Diploma curriculum](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/) , students take six subjects and may replace the arts subject with another science, language, or individuals and societies subject. This allows Biology and Chemistry within a regular Diploma.


Taking Biology, Chemistry, and Physics can be more complicated. The IB identifies medicine in countries including India, Pakistan, and some Scandinavian countries as a possible reason to consider a **non-regular Diploma** . Its illustrative non-regular medicine combination includes all three sciences at HL with Mathematics AA SL.


Students cannot independently declare a non-regular Diploma. It requires school involvement and IB authorization because the intended university course must leave no suitable regular alternative. Discuss this route with your IB coordinator early and confirm current eligibility rules with the relevant university and national professional authority.

These are planning models, not guaranteed admission routes. Eligibility may also depend on grades, admissions tests, interviews, language requirements, written applications, and contextual criteria.


### Common subject-selection mistakes


**Choosing before researching destinations** is risky because medical education differs internationally. The United Kingdom offers direct entry from secondary school, whereas medicine in the United States and much of Canada normally follows an undergraduate degree. Pre-medical undergraduate requirements are not necessarily identical to direct-entry Medicine requirements.


**Assuming the hardest combination is strongest** can damage overall performance. The IB permits three or four HL subjects, but four HLs do not automatically impress admissions teams. Excess workload can affect internal assessments, TOK, the Extended Essay, admissions-test preparation, and final grades.


**Treating a science Extended Essay as a requirement** is another misconception. A Biology or Chemistry EE can develop research skills, but it does not replace required subjects or grades. Choose one only when the question, supervision, evidence, and method are manageable.


Finally, avoid relying on outdated summaries. Use the[IB university recognition database](https://recognition.ibo.org/en-US/) for initial research, but treat the university's current course page as the decisive source.


### A practical decision process


1.


**Identify likely countries and pathways.** Determine whether you are targeting direct-entry or graduate-entry medicine.


2.


**Create a university shortlist.** Include realistic medical programmes and several backup degrees.


3.


**Record formal conditions.** Separate required subjects and grades from recommendations.


4.


**Place mandatory sciences at HL.** For broad flexibility, this usually means Biology and Chemistry.


5.


**Choose the third HL strategically.** Consider university conditions, backup courses, and academic strengths.


6.


**Check mathematics precisely.** Record the accepted course and level rather than assuming AA or HL is compulsory.


7.


**Evaluate the full workload.** Include laboratory work, internal assessments, TOK, the EE, CAS, and admissions tests.


8.


**Confirm school availability.** Timetable blocks and staffing may restrict otherwise valid combinations.


9.


**Recheck requirements before applying.** Admissions policies can change after subject selection.


Students can preview course depth through the[RevisionDojo IB subject hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib) ,[IB Biology resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-biology-new) , and[IB Chemistry resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-chemistry-new) . The[Biology Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-biology-new/questionbank) and[Chemistry Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-chemistry-new/questionbank) can also help assess readiness for sustained HL study.


### Conclusion


For the widest access to undergraduate medicine, choose **Biology HL and Chemistry HL** , then select a third HL that meets remaining prerequisites and supports a high total score. Mathematics or Physics HL may be necessary for particular universities, but neither is a universal requirement.


Build a shortlist first, verify every condition on official admissions pages, and discuss unusual combinations with your IB coordinator. Once subjects are confirmed, RevisionDojo Study Notes, Questionbanks, Flashcards, and Jojo AI can support consistent Biology and Chemistry practice.
